name: JW Marriott Marco Island Beach Resort
positioning: Balinese-inspired beach resort with its own stretch of private Gulf beach on Marco Island, Florida, including the 21-and-over Paradise by Sirene retreat
best_for: Families who want a beach resort with a kids' day camp
Couples who want a retreat reserved for guests 21 and over
Golfers and travelers who want Gulf and Everglades excursions

facts.text: The resort is Balinese-inspired in its design.
The resort has its own stretch of private beach on the Gulf.
Marco Island sits at the northern point of the Florida Gulf Coast's Ten Thousand Islands.
Paradise by Sirene is a retreat within the resort reserved for guests ages 21 and over.
Paradise by Sirene guests receive a complimentary continental breakfast for two each morning.
The Presidential Suites have a wrap-around terrace with panoramic, unobstructed views of the Gulf.
Spa by JW offers massages, facials, body treatments and nail services.
The fitness center offers classes including beach yoga.
The Tiki Time Day Camp is for kids ages 5 to 10, with games, crafts and lunch.
The resort has two championship golf courses, including Hammock Bay, a par 72 Audubon gold-certified sanctuary course designed by Peter Jacobsen and Jim Hardy.
Guests can head out on the Gulf by catamaran in search of dolphins, manatees and sea turtles.
The resort has 12 food and beverage outlets.

highlights.text: Paradise by Sirene guests have a rooftop pool reserved for adults.
The resort stages a complimentary daily Balinese-inspired fire dancer performance at sunset.
Balinese-inspired Beach Chickee Huts give a shaded retreat on the beach for up to six guests.
The one-story Lanai Suites sit next to Quinn's pool, a few steps from the sand.
Airboat tours glide through the mangrove forest of the Ten Thousand Islands.

considerations.text: The championship golf courses are not at the resort; they are about 15 minutes away.
Southwest Florida International Airport is 48 miles from the resort.
Pets are not allowed at the resort.
